record.who: Customers on the Advanced (formerly Enterprise) plan, plus anyone on Lite or standalone Outbound Essentials, which are no longer offered. Whether existing customers are repriced is not stated.

record.headline: Render doubled the maximum compute for a Workflows task to 8 CPU/32 GB, priced the new 8c-32g tier at $2.50/hour, and replaced concurrent-run limits with parallel compute limits.
record.who: Customers of Render Workflows; the compute-table change applies to all plans that can run Workflows.
record.read: Workflows is moving from a concurrency-based allowance to a compute-based one, which ties cost more closely to resources used. The larger task size and the end of the per-50 concurrency fee make this look like a loosening, though the exact effect on a given bill depends on usage.
record.caveat: PricingSaaS history shows Workflows max compute going up and down over recent weeks, so this may not be settled.
